12.0.0.en: 1 For Your incorruptible Spirit is in all things. 2 Therefore You rebuke sinners little by little, and in what they sin You remind them and warn them, that they may turn away from evil and believe in You, O Lord.

12.0.1.en: For Your incorruptible Spirit is in all things. [1]

12.0.2.en: God promised His people the land of promise, but He does not compel the peoples who dwell in the land. He rebuked them little by little, because He is a lover of all men, and seeks their repentance and their immortality. They are His beloved creation whose incorruption He seeks.

12.0.3.en: "Your incorruptible Spirit": the Spirit of God gives eternal life to the creation, and takes no pleasure in its corruption and destruction, because He Himself is incorruptible.

12.0.4.en: The Spirit of God fills the whole world, and He is holy, sanctifying and untouched by corruption. He desires to work in all, but not by compulsion. He works in unbelievers that they may believe, and in believers that they may bear the fruit of the Spirit (Gal 5:22).

12.0.5.en: By "all things" here he means all mankind, for in every man there is a spark from God, the breath of life that God gave to Adam (Gen 2:7), that all his offspring might enjoy it.

12.0.6.en: * The Son and the Holy Spirit are the source of sanctification, by them every rational creature is sanctified according to its readiness.

12.0.7.en: * The Holy Spirit, who proceeds from God (the Father), is the source of holiness, the life-giving power, the grace that bestows perfection; through Him man enjoys adoption, the corruptible becomes incorruption; He is one with the Father and the Son in everything, in glory and eternity and power and kingdom and divinity; this is experienced by the tradition of the baptism of salvation.

12.0.8.en: * This is our renewal, making us again in the image of God, by the washing of regeneration and the Holy Spirit who renews us so that we become sons of God, we become a new creation again by the fellowship of the Spirit, and He saves us from what was old.

12.0.9.en: * By the washing of the new birth and the renewal by the Holy Spirit we become sons of God.

12.0.10.en: * The new life is the life that the Gospel described and that Christ lived on earth, and this requires of man meekness and patience and endurance and purity of heart and body and detachment from wealth. Thus the life of the blessed in heaven is realized on earth. And it must be remembered that the Holy Spirit is the worker and the essential mover in this renewal of life, and in its changing into a life with Christ. For it is He who moves us to call God our true Father; and it is He who makes us partakers of the great graces of redemption; and it is He who makes us, as St. John says, sons of the light, sharing thus in the eternal glory that is about to be revealed in us. And in a brief word, the Holy Spirit is He who makes us possess all that God wishes us to possess, and to understand by faith the promises of what we shall possess in the other life.

12.0.11.en: * By the Holy Spirit is the restoration of our dwelling in Paradise, our ascent to the Kingdom of Heaven, our return to divine sonship, our boldness to call God "our Father," our sharing in the grace of Christ, our being called sons of light, our right to eternal glory, and in one word our obtaining the fullness of blessing in this age and in the age to come.

12.1.0.en: St. Basil the Great Therefore You rebuke little by little those who err, and warn them, reminding them of what they sin in, that they may turn away from evil and trust in You, O Lord. [2]

12.1.1.en: In His chastening of men He rebukes them little by little, that they may perhaps return to Him, for He takes no pleasure in the destruction of the living (Gen 1:23).

12.1.2.en: St. Augustine sees that God does not punish every sin we commit, but only a very small number of our sins, so that even through this punishment or chastening we perceive His care for us, and keep in mind the Last Judgment.

12.1.3.en: If God chastens little by little, it is because He wants us to experience the bitterness of sin, and to flee from eternal punishment by returning to Him and clinging to Him.

12.1.4.en: * Paul rightly said that the wrath of God is revealed... in this present time. God refrains from carrying out the full punishment, so as not to take away the opportunity of repentance, which leads to the return of (sinners) so that they are saved, or to their departing (from God) and having no excuse.

12.1.5.en: Theodore, Bishop of Mopsuestia The wise man addresses the question of some, perhaps they were of the Gentile kings his friends: Why did God pour out harsh plagues on Pharaoh and his people, and also on the original inhabitants of Canaan?

12.1.6.en: The wise man reveals the plan of God, that this did not happen out of partiality toward a certain people, nor out of any divine hatred against some people or nation, for He desires that all be sanctified, and enjoy divine power. So the goal of the divine rebuke and chastening that follows is:

12.1.7.en: a. To remind sinners of their sins, therefore the kind of chastening often carries a disclosure of certain sins.

12.1.8.en: b. God seeks to make sin bitter in their mouths, so that they may cease from it.

12.1.9.en: c. Sinners realize their weakness and take refuge in God the source of their strength, and trust in Him. For every rebuke or chastening carries not hatred, but feelings of love for the edification of those under chastening or punishment.

12.2.s.en: 2. God's forbearance in His dealing with Canaan

12.2.0.en: 3 For You hated those who were of old the inhabitants of Your holy land, 4 for their works that were hateful to You, of sorcery and unholy sacrifices, 5 since they killed their children without mercy, and ate the entrails of men, and drank their blood in the rites of Your worship. 6 So You were pleased to destroy by the hands of our fathers those parents, murderers of helpless souls, 7 that the land which is most precious to You of all lands might be filled with the children of God, as is worthy of it. 8 Yet You spared those also, because they were men, and sent wasps as forerunners of Your army, to destroy them little by little, 9 not because You were unable to subdue the hypocrites to the righteous in battle, or to destroy them at once by ravenous beasts, or by a stern word from You, 10 but by punishing them little by little You gave them a chance to repent, though it was not hidden from You that their generation was wicked, and their malice innate, and their thoughts would never change, 11 for they were a cursed seed from the beginning. And it was not through fear of anyone that You granted pardon for their sins, and as for those who were of old the inhabitants of Your holy land, [3]

12.3.0.en: You hated them for their abominable works, of sorcery and defiled rites. [4]

12.3.1.en: The hatred here is directed not against the wicked themselves, but against the sin with which they ally themselves, so that they fall under the natural judgment and the fruit of sin. As though the wicked drink from the very cup that they fill for themselves. For the battle is between divine holiness and evil.

12.3.2.en: * Whoever wallows in a pit full of mire and sinks into it falls into the snares of vanity (and delivers himself to destruction).

12.3.3.en: St. Ambrose * Who can say to God: Why do You judge the world (that is in sin)? How can God the just Judge be accused when the guilt of the world is condemned?

12.3.4.en: St. Augustine And the killing of children without mercy.

12.4.0.en: And banquets of flesh and human blood, in which they eat even the entrails. [5]

12.4.1.en: What grieves the heart of God is that man in his practice of (pagan) worship is turned into a ravening beast, for the Canaanites used to offer human sacrifices to Baal (Jer 19:5), and they made their children pass through the fire, offering them to the priests, who in turn threw them onto bronze statues blazing with fire, amid the loud beating of drums. And as St. John Chrysostom says, wild animals do not devour those of their own kind, but man devours his brother and kills him.

12.4.2.en: Among their rites also was the eating of the flesh of human sacrifices in ritual feasts.

12.4.3.en: Perhaps Jephthah the Gileadite was influenced by such customs, which led him to make a hasty vow to offer as a sacrifice the first who met him, and she was his only daughter (Judg 11:39).

12.4.4.en: God, the lover of all mankind, cannot bear these savage deeds.

12.5.0.en: With their priests as part of the pagan staff, and the parents who themselves murdered helpless souls, You willed to destroy them by the hands of our fathers. [6]

12.5.1.en: Perhaps some will ask: Why did God allow the Canaanites to be killed by the Israelites? The wise man answers: Why do you condemn God for the killing of people who kill their own children, who have no one to defend them and no power to resist them? The cry of these innocent children went up against their parents, and evil reached its utmost, therefore God allowed their killing not all at once, but group by group, that perhaps they might turn from their evils.

12.6.0.en: That the land which is most precious to You of all lands might be filled with the children of God, as is worthy of it. [7]

12.6.1.en: Since the pagans did not turn back from their evils, He wanted His people to take their place, that they might be a holy leaven for the believers in the whole world, by the coming of the Savior of the world incarnate from them.

12.7.0.en: Yet You spared those also because they were men, and sent wasps as forerunners of Your army, to destroy them little by little. [8]

12.7.1.en: God in His long-suffering was sparing these pagan nations, so He did not crush them, nor did He allow beasts to devour them all at once, but He allows their expulsion or killing gradually that perhaps they may return to Him.

12.7.2.en: By wasps in the Holy Scripture is often meant an instrument of chastening, especially by allowing the attack of enemy armies to trouble them. It is said in the book of the prophet Isaiah: "And it shall come to pass in that day, that the LORD shall hiss for the fly in the land of Assyria" (Isa 7:18).

12.8.0.en: Not because You were unable to deliver the wicked into the hands of the righteous in battle, or to destroy them at once by ravenous beasts, or by a stern word. [9]

12.8.1.en: He could have destroyed the pagans with one blow from the believers, as happened with the army of Sennacherib, but He keeps giving opportunities for them to reconsider themselves.

12.8.2.en: But by carrying out Your judgment little by little, You gave them a chance to repent, though it was not hidden from You that their nature was wicked.

12.9.0.en: And that their malice was innate, and their mentality would never change. [10]

12.9.1.en: Here he speaks of the Canaanites in general as tribes and small states that had drunk in evil from generation to generation, until the evils mingled with their nature, and controlled their thoughts, and made them lose even the affection of motherhood and fatherhood. But without doubt there existed a few who longed, by the natural law, to know the truth and to enjoy eternal life. This few, who were almost counted as nothing before the multitude of the wicked, God did not forget, as happened in Egypt at the departure of Moses the prophet and those with him.

12.9.2.en: This few of the Egyptians was called the mixed multitude, as stated in the book of Exodus: "And a mixed multitude went up also with them; and flocks, and herds, even very much cattle" (Ex 38:12). Among this mixed multitude were those who went out with the Hebrews with a living faith in God, and some who attached themselves to them merely because they were dazzled by the signs and wonders that Moses performed. And the latter group was a cause of the Hebrews' falling into weaknesses in the wilderness (Num 4:11).

12.9.3.en: As for the Canaanites, among them also were those who accepted faith in God, and were called "proselytes." And there were proselytes among the Jews until the age of the Apostles (Acts 2:10; 13:43).

12.9.4.en: * Let us look to the generations of old, and learn that the Lord - from generation to generation - offers a chance to repent to those who wish to return to Him.

12.9.5.en: Noah preached repentance, and those who listened to him were saved.

12.9.6.en: Jonah proclaimed the destruction of the people of Nineveh, and when they repented of their sins they propitiated God by prayer, and obtained salvation although they were strangers to the (covenant of) God.

12.9.7.en: By the Holy Spirit the ministers of the grace of God spoke of repentance.

12.9.8.en: And the Lord of all Himself spoke with an oath, saying: "As I live, saith the Lord, I desire not the death of the sinner, but his repentance" (Ezek 32:11 LXX), and then He adds this good counsel: "Repent, O house of Israel, of your evil deeds, say to the sons of My people, though your sins reach from the earth to heaven, and though they become redder than scarlet, and blacker than sackcloth of mourning, and you turn to Me with all your hearts, saying: "O Father," I will hear you as a holy people.

12.9.9.en: St. Clement of Rome * He (Wisdom) calls the good and the wicked to enter, in order to strengthen the good and to transfer the wicked to a better state. This saying has been fulfilled today, namely that "the wolf and the lamb shall feed together" (Isa 65:25).

12.9.10.en: He calls the poor and the maimed and the blind; by this He shows that we who are disabled are not excluded from the Kingdom of Heaven... He sends them to the highways (Mt 22:9), because wisdom sings with a loud voice in the passages (Prov 1:20). He sends them to the streets, for He sends them to sinners that they may come from the broad ways to the narrow way that leads to life (Mt 7:13-14). He sends them to the public roads and the hedged areas, those who are not occupied with any desire for temporal things, but hasten toward the way of the good will.

12.9.11.en: St. Ambrose * The people of Nineveh became wicked, and God judged them that "Nineveh shall be overthrown" (see Jon 3:4).

12.9.12.en: God did not want to issue a sentence without doing anything, but wanted to give them a chance to repent and change, therefore He sent a Hebrew prophet, so that when he says: "Nineveh shall be overthrown," the sentence is not carried out, but they obtain the mercy of God by repentance.

12.9.13.en: * God, who judges little by little those who are punished, gives them a chance to repent (Wis 12:10). And not punishing them at once for everything stops the punishment of the sinner.

12.9.14.en: Origen For they were a cursed seed from the beginning.

12.10.0.en: And it was not through fear of anyone that You granted pardon for their sins. [11]

12.10.1.en: * As human beings, their nature is good, which God brought into being and made; but since they are born in sin, and appointed to destruction unless they are born again, they belong to the seed that was cursed from the beginning by the fault of the disobedience of the first parents.

12.10.2.en: In any case, this fault was turned to good by the Creator Himself for the vessels of wrath, that He might make known the riches of His glory in the vessels of mercy (Rom 9:33), so that no one may ascribe merit to himself... but salvation is accomplished by grace, so whoever boasts, let him boast in the Lord (2 Cor 10:17).

12.10.3.en: * In truth, if the seed bears no corruption in it, what does the statement in the book of Wisdom mean: "And it was not hidden from You that their nature was wicked, and their malice innate, and their mentality would never change, for they were a cursed seed from the beginning" (see Wis 12:10-11)?

12.10.4.en: Now even if this was used of a particular case, these words speak of what concerns mankind.

12.10.5.en: Then how can the malice of every man be innate, and his seed cursed from the beginning, unless it concerns the truth that: "by one man sin entered into the world, and death by sin; and so death passed upon all men, in whom all sinned" (Rom 5:12)?

12.11.s.en: 3. A God who cares for all

12.11.0.en: 12 For who will say, What have You done? or resist Your judgment? And who will accuse You for the destruction of nations that You made, or stand before You as an advocate for unrighteous men? 13 For there is no God but You, who care for all, that You may show that You do not judge unjustly, for who is it that says: What have You done?

12.11.2.en: And who will bring You to trial because You destroyed the nations that You created?

12.11.3.en: Or who will come before You to plead for unrighteous men? [12]

12.11.4.en: It is a wonder that man should overstep his bounds to take the position of a critic of the actions of God. Instead of condemning himself for his evils, and criticizing mankind for its deviation, in boldness and folly he says to God: What have You done? objecting to God's judgment, accusing Him of injustice and violence and harshness.

12.11.5.en: God who judges for the wronged, breaking the jaws of the unrighteous (Job 17:29), delivering His children from the unrighteous man (Ps 48:18), is accused of injustice.

12.12.0.en: For there is no God but You who care for all men, that You may show that You do not judge unjustly. [13]

12.12.1.en: The wise man often affirms that God is the God of all men, who cares for all, and will not judge unjustly. The doors of His mercies are open to all nations and peoples, if they return to Him they find the divine embrace waiting for them and delighting in them. Perhaps the mission of Jonah the prophet to the people of Nineveh, and God's attitude toward their repentance, is among the most wonderful examples of God's love for all mankind without partiality.

12.12.2.en: And many of the prophets in the Old Testament called the pagan peoples to return to God to enjoy His work, that they might rejoice and praise Him.

12.12.3.en: "Let the people praise thee, O God; let all the people praise thee" (Ps 67:3).

12.12.4.en: "O let the nations be glad and sing for joy: for thou shalt judge the people righteously, and govern the nations upon earth. Selah" (Ps 67:4).

12.12.5.en: "Let the people praise thee, O God; let all the people praise thee" (Ps 67:5).

12.12.6.en: "Declare his glory among the heathen, his wonders among all people" (Ps 96:3).

12.12.7.en: "Give unto the LORD, O ye kindreds of the people, give unto the LORD glory and strength" (Ps 96:7).

12.12.8.en: "When the people are gathered together, and the kingdoms, to serve the LORD" (Ps 102:22).

12.12.9.en: "And love the light of wisdom, O rulers of the peoples" (Wis 6:23).

12.12.10.en: "Behold, I have made him a lawgiver to the people, a leader and commander to the people" (Isa 55:4).

12.12.11.en: "Even them will I bring to my holy mountain, and make them joyful in my house of prayer: their burnt offerings and their sacrifices shall be accepted upon mine altar; for mine house shall be called an house of prayer for all people" (Isa 56:7).

12.12.12.en: "And many people shall go and say, Come ye, and let us go up to the mountain of the LORD, to the house of the God of Jacob; and he will teach us of his ways, and we will walk in his paths: for out of Zion shall go forth the law, and the word of the LORD from Jerusalem" (Isa 2:3).

12.12.13.en: "And he shall judge among the nations, and shall do justice for many people: and they shall beat their swords into plowshares, and their spears into pruninghooks: nation shall not lift up sword against nation, neither shall they learn war any more" (Isa 2:4).

12.12.14.en: "Before I formed thee in the belly I knew thee; and before thou camest forth out of the womb I sanctified thee, and I ordained thee a prophet unto the nations" (Jer 1:5).

12.12.15.en: St. Mar Jacob of Serugh portrays for us the surpassing love of God. For if the wicked drink from the cup of their evil bitterness and eternal destruction, then God in His love allows the revelation of His wrath against their sins, not for vengeance nor for their destruction, but to reveal to them the fruit of their evil. By this He calls them to repentance that they may enjoy His tenderness, so that the doors of wrath are closed upon them, and the doors of heaven are opened to welcome them.

12.12.16.en: He likens the sinner to a sleeping girl, whom God awakens with His threats, so that destruction may not come upon her suddenly!

12.12.17.en: * The revelation from God came to the prophet (Jonah), that he might go and bring the Gentile peoples back to repentance.

12.12.18.en: He sent him to Nineveh to proclaim the overturning of her goods, so that by her threatening the evils might be abolished.

12.12.19.en: He said to him: Arise, go, and preach there to the people of Nineveh, and speak in their ears the preaching that I tell you...

12.12.20.en: If God had wanted to strike Nineveh because of the multitude of her iniquities, He would not have sent to her that she might turn away from evils.

12.12.21.en: If He had set His face to harm her in truth, He would have sent wrath suddenly and struck her.

12.12.22.en: He sent to her that she might feel the situation, and seek the mercies that would save her.

12.12.23.en: He raised His hand to strike and destroy the sleeper, and He called her and awakened her, that she might not be struck in her sleep...

12.12.24.en: Zeal for justice awoke against the wretched one, and He sent to her by grace that she might awake by repentance.

12.12.25.en: Wrath went forth against the city to destroy it, and tenderness came forward and shut the doors before wrath, so it did not enter.

12.12.26.en: Were it not for the existence of these mercies, what need would there be to send the preacher.

12.12.27.en: He sent him to the place to turn it back from evils, and by repentance it has rest, and corruption does not come.

12.12.28.en: St. Jacob of Serugh The Gentile sailors were able to enter the house of God while in the ship in the midst of the sea, and offered sacrifices of praise and thanksgiving acceptable to God, and enjoyed the fear of the Lord (Jon 1:16), of which many of the people of God deprived themselves.

12.12.29.en: * The sailors looked at the sea, and it had become silent from its waves, so they increased in fear of God the Lord of the seas... They realized from the wonder that had happened that the whirlwinds had been sent after Jonah. They understood the work with discernment, that the Lord had commanded the waves of the sea and they obeyed Him. By faith they realized that the Lord is in the sea, so they offered sacrifices, and vowed vows with great love.

12.12.30.en: They entered among the people of the house of Adonai (God) and took refuge in Him, and began to offer perfect sacrifices there.

12.13.0.en: 14 And there is no king or ruler who can demand an account from You of those whom You destroyed. 15 And since You are just, You govern all things with justice, and consider it contrary to Your power to condemn one who does not deserve punishment. 16 For Your strength is the source of Your justice, and since You are Lord of all, You spare all. 17 And You show Your strength to those who do not believe that You are perfect in power, and You punish the boldness of those who know it. 18 But You, O mighty Ruler, judge with gentleness, and govern us with much sparing, for it is in Your hand to act with power whenever You will.

12.13.1.en: And no king or ruler can confront You concerning those whom You punished. [14]

12.13.2.en: God the Almighty is just in His judgments, there is no one who can confront Him in the matter of punishing the wicked who persist in their evil.

12.13.3.en: "He is the Rock, his work is perfect: for all his ways are judgment: a God of truth and without iniquity, just and right is he" (Deut 32:4).

12.13.4.en: "And he said: Righteous art thou, O Lord, and all thy judgments are right, and all thy ways are mercy and truth and judgment" (Tob 3:2).

12.13.5.en: "God is a righteous judge, and a God that hath indignation every day" (Ps 7:11).

12.13.6.en: "For thou hast maintained my right and my cause; thou satest in the throne judging right" (Ps 9:4).

12.13.7.en: "For the righteous LORD loveth righteousness; his countenance doth behold the upright" (Ps 11:7).

12.13.8.en: "The fear of the LORD is clean, enduring for ever: the judgments of the LORD are true and righteous altogether" (Ps 19:9).

12.13.9.en: "The righteousness of thy testimonies is everlasting: give me understanding, and I shall live" (Ps 119:144).

12.13.10.en: "Therefore the LORD hath watched over the evil, and brought it upon us: for the LORD is righteous in all his works which he hath commanded us" (Bar 2:9).

12.13.11.en: For thou art just in all that thou hast done, and all thy works are true, and thy ways right, and all thy judgments truth" (Dan 3:27).

12.13.12.en: "The just LORD is in the midst thereof; he will not do iniquity: every morning doth he bring his judgment to light, he faileth not; but the unjust knoweth no shame" (Zeph 3:5).

12.13.13.en: "Rejoice greatly, O daughter of Zion; shout, O daughter of Jerusalem: behold, thy King cometh unto thee: he is just, and having salvation; lowly, and riding upon an ass, and upon a colt the foal of an ass" (Zech 9:9).

12.13.14.en: "And this is what Nehemiah prayed: O Lord, Lord God, Creator of all things, fearful, and strong, and righteous, and merciful, who alone art King and righteous" (2 Macc 1:24).

12.13.15.en: "Who alone art gracious, just, almighty, and everlasting, thou that deliverest Israel from all evil, who didst choose the fathers, and sanctify them" (2 Macc 1:25).

12.13.16.en: * Some bring false accusations against God, or rather against the books of the Old Testament... No one doubts that the will of God is wholly just.

12.13.17.en: St. Augustine * Paul says that it is wrong to say that God is unjust because of His wrath against men. For how can one who judges the world be thought unjust, since his very title "Judge" shows that He does nothing without judgment, and where judgment exists, consequently justice exists. For the two words "judge" and "judgment" are derived (in Greek) from "justice."

12.13.18.en: Justice and injustice are natural enemies - so how can God be regarded as unjust merely because He fights injustice?

12.14.0.en: Origen And since You are righteous, You govern all in righteousness, and count it contrary to Your power to judge one who does not deserve punishment. [15]

12.14.1.en: God the Creator of all mankind, in His love for all and His justice, shows partiality to no one, for all are equal before Him. Truly there is no being that can stand before Him or review His judgments, but in His divine justice He judges everyone according to his deserving.

12.14.2.en: * Whoever doubts this, let him read what Peter said when he visited the Gentile Cornelius: "Of a truth I perceive that God is no respecter of persons: but in every nation he that feareth him, and worketh righteousness, is accepted with him" (Acts 34:10-35). We must go further than that, and quote what our Lord says in the Gospel: "He that believeth on me is not condemned: but he that believeth not is condemned already, because he hath not believed in the name of the only begotten Son of God" (Jn 18:3).

12.14.3.en: Origen * God shows no partiality to persons; He judges works.

12.14.4.en: St. John Chrysostom * We were all born equal, emperors and common people, and we die equal. Our humanity is of one kind.

12.14.5.en: St. Jerome For Your strength is the source of Your righteousness.

12.15.0.en: And since You are Lord of all, You spare all. [16]

12.15.1.en: God as an everlasting example to the sons of men presents to us a true concept of leadership and governance, for it is said:

12.15.2.en: "Since You are Lord of all, You spare all men" (Wis 12:16).

12.15.3.en: "But You, being master of Your strength, judge with gentleness" (Wis 12:18).

12.15.4.en: So we see in God our Leader that lordship is joined with compassion, and power with gentleness. For the living leader is the one who rules by his love and tenderness and gentleness, not only over those he shepherds, but over all men. For love has no limits!

12.15.5.en: Even in His chastening God deals gently with all men, and desires that they enjoy His mercy.

12.15.6.en: You display Your strength when men doubt the perfection of Your power.

12.16.0.en: And You put to shame the boldness of those who know it. [17]

12.16.1.en: When God displays His strength, He does not display it as a kind of show to obtain some glory, nor to terrify His creation. But He displays it before unbelievers that they may accept Him and so enjoy His power, and that the ignorant who had not realized the divine possibilities may recognize it.

12.16.2.en: He also displays it before those who know it intellectually or mentally without having experienced it in their practical life; He displays it that they may be put to shame, and their knowledge may turn into an experience of life with the Almighty.

12.17.0.en: But You, being master of Your strength, judge with gentleness, and govern us with much sparing, for power is in Your hand to act whenever You will. [18]

12.17.1.en: Again, since we know that God is the Almighty, His power is for the enjoyment of His tenderness and kindness, and His lordship or authority is for the ordering of our life and working for our edification. If we respond to Him, His power appears through His free grace that He gives to His believers, so they glorify the Almighty God working in them. Thus many of the Fathers link the power of God with His grace.

12.17.2.en: * Draw near, beloved, to faith, for its powers are very many. Faith (Enoch) took up to heaven, and overcame the flood, and made the barren woman bear. It delivered from the sword, and brought up from the pit, enriched the poor, and loosed the captives, delivered the persecuted, and quenched fire, and cleft the sea, and shook the rock, and gave the thirsty water to drink, and satisfied the hungry. It raised the dead and brought them out of Hades, and calmed the waves, and healed the sick. It conquered enemies and destroyed fortresses. It stopped the mouths of lions, and quenched the flame of fire. It brought down the proud and honored the humble. All these mighty works faith has done.

12.18.s.en: 5. God a model for His people

12.18.0.en: 19 So by these works of Yours You taught Your people that the righteous man must be a lover of men, and You gave Your sons a good hope, because You grant them in their sins a time for repentance. 20 For if You punished the enemies of Your sons, who deserved death, with such care and gentleness, and gave them time and place to turn from evil, 21 with what care did You govern Your sons, whose fathers You bound with oaths and covenants to Your good promises? 22 So You chasten us, and scourge our enemies with many stripes, that we may remember Your forbearance when we judge, and wait for Your mercy when we are judged.

12.18.1.en: And by these Your works You taught Your people that the righteous man must be gentle, and You gave Your children good hope, because You grant repentance for sins. [19]

12.18.2.en: God presents Himself as an example and a model of gentleness toward all men. "Leaving us an example, that ye should follow his steps" (1 Pet 2:21).

12.18.3.en: The true righteous man bears the Spirit of God and so loves all, and does not despair of the salvation of anyone, for God grants repentance for sins to those who long for the knowledge of the truth or for eternal salvation.

12.18.4.en: Repentance is a gift from God, and not a purely human work, in which a man calls himself to account by himself. For this reckoning may lead to remorse without hope in the mercies of God, as happened with Judas who, because of the weight of his sense of guilt, hanged himself.

12.18.5.en: What did God teach His people through His dealings even with the wicked?

12.18.6.en: a. By His tenderness toward the wicked, and chastening them gradually and not all at once, He taught us to bear His Spirit, and so to love all men, even those who oppose us [19].

12.19.0.en: b. God has a certain plan whether in His tenderness or in His chastenings, affirming that for everything there is the suitable place and the fitting time, so we do not hasten God in His chastening of the wicked [20].

12.20.0.en: c. God remains faithful and fulfills His promises that He made to the fathers, even if He chastens the sons [21].

12.21.0.en: d. In the midst of the slow chastening of our opponents we fix our eyes on the mercies of God, so we do not despair and our souls are not shattered [22]. For if God is gentle with opponents, scourging them little, let us remember how very long-suffering He is with us, so we are filled with hope that we shall enjoy His mercy on the Day of Judgment.

12.21.1.en: For those who were enemies of Your sons, and deserved death, if You punished them with such care and indulgence, giving them time and opportunity to turn from their evil. [20]

12.21.2.en: The wise man uses every means to draw us to long-suffering toward the wicked, for God Himself the Judge, even in His punishing the wicked here, chastens them with gentleness and indulgence, waiting for the time of their repentance. In the comment of St. Mar Jacob of Serugh on God's threat of the destruction of Nineveh, he shows how He judges so that man may appeal his case, presenting sincere repentance with humility as an intercessor before the court of God, and God then proclaims not only his innocence, but also divine pleasure in this innocence.

12.21.3.en: * Death is estrangement from God and being cut off from Him; and life is immortality, and peace is fellowship with Him.

12.21.4.en: Gennadius, Bishop of Constantinople With what exactness You judged Your sons, to whose fathers You made promises with oaths and covenants full of true promises? [21]

12.21.5.en: If God is gentle in this way even with those who trouble His people, how much more does He have compassion on His children who cling to Him, and who have put their trust in His promises.

12.21.6.en: And so, when You chasten us by scourging our enemies a thousand times, that we may remember Your forbearance when we judge, and wait for Your mercy when we are judged. [22]

12.21.7.en: However harsh and bitter the chastenings that come upon the wicked may seem, they are counted very light if compared with what he will suffer on the last day if he does not repent.

12.21.8.en: The earnest believer in his life looks upon God's chastenings of the wicked as long-suffering, because God waits for their repentance and return, so that they may not fall under eternal punishment. They are a lesson for the wicked themselves as for the righteous.

12.22.s.en: 6. Sin bears its punishment within it

12.22.0.en: 23 Therefore the hypocrites who lived in folly, You tormented with their very abominations, 24 for in their error they went beyond the ways of error, taking as gods those of the animals that their enemies despise, deceived like children who do not understand. 25 Therefore You sent upon them, as upon children without reason, a punishment of mockery. 26 And when they were not admonished by the chastening of mockery, they tasted the punishment worthy of God. 27 And in what they endured in their indignation, when they saw that those whom they had taken as gods were tormenting them, they knew the true God, whom they had denied; and therefore the final punishment came upon them.

12.22.1.en: Therefore those who lived in folly an unrighteous life, You tormented with the abominations of their own souls. [23]

12.22.2.en: He returns to speak of His chastening of the Egyptians gradually, and affirms the following:

12.23.0.en: a. That He looks upon the wicked as children without understanding. He began first with mockery, how they worship animals, even contemptible insects, of which they made gods [24-25].

12.24.0.en: b. Since they did not heed the mockery they fell under harsher chastenings [26-27], ending with the killing of the firstborn and the drowning of Pharaoh and his army in the sea.

12.24.1.en: This book often makes clear that the troubles that come upon the sinner, though by God's permission for his chastening, are the natural fruit of the corruption that sin brings. Sin itself bears the germ of corruption, and bears bitterness within it.

12.24.2.en: * One question remains that needs an answer: Do you live in this world in godliness or in evil? If you do not live in godliness you must not wonder if the shepherds chasten you here, even if you do not suffer from us, but God Himself chastens you with the vileness of your souls.

12.24.3.en: St. Augustine For in their error they went beyond the ways of error, taking as gods those of the animals that their enemies despise, deceived like children who do not understand. [24]

12.24.4.en: We saw how the Egyptians fell into the worship of animals and even of the weak insects; they fell in foolishness, like children without wisdom in this worship.

12.24.5.en: Therefore You sent upon them, as upon children without reason, a judgment of mockery. [25]

12.24.6.en: Since the Egyptians worshiped irrational animals, irrationality was poured upon them, and they became an object of mockery.

12.24.7.en: They thought they were able to practice powers and wonders by magicians, and the magicians stood helpless before the plagues that came upon Pharaoh and his people.

12.24.8.en: * The tyrant Pharaoh tried to meet the divine signs that Moses and Aaron displayed with magic tricks performed by his magicians (Ex 7:1-12). And when Moses changed his rod a second time into a serpent before the eyes of the Egyptians, they thought that the magic of the magicians could produce similar miracles with their rods. But this was proved to be a deception when the serpent that was the rod of Moses ate the rods of the magicians - which appeared like serpents - but they had no means of defending themselves nor any power of life, but were only a deceptive appearance, skillfully counterfeited by the magicians before those who were easy to deceive.

12.24.9.en: St. Gregory of Nyssa But those who were not admonished by the chastening of mockery tasted the judgment worthy of God. [26]

12.24.10.en: It was fitting for Pharaoh and his men to reconsider their position after they became an object of mockery, and were in a position of weakness. But they insisted on continuing in their stubbornness, and followed the track of Moses and his people, and even wanted to cross after them by the same road that appeared in the midst of the waters of the Red Sea, so they perished.

12.24.11.en: * He presented to us what concerns the Exodus of Israel that we may know those who are saved by Baptism... The sea is a type of Baptism, so it saved the people from Pharaoh as you are saved from the tyranny of the devil in Baptism. The sea destroyed the enemy, and in Baptism our enmity toward God is killed. The people came out of the sea whole and safe, and we also come out of the water like the living coming out from among the dead.

12.25.0.en: St. Basil the Great They were indignant at those beasts that tormented them, and saw that they were punished by those whom they had counted gods, so they knew the true God whom they had denied, and therefore the final punishment came upon them. [27]

12.25.1.en: The final punishment after the ten plagues is their drowning in the Red Sea as a type of eternal destruction in the lake burning with fire, and they cast themselves into it in folly and recklessness.

12.25.2.en: Grant me Your wisdom, O divine Leader

12.25.3.en: * You are the wonderful divine Leader!

12.25.4.en: I see You, without partiality, tender toward all.

12.25.5.en: You are gentle with Your believers, and in Your fatherhood You also chasten.

12.25.6.en: Your love radiates from Your kindness as from Your firmness.

12.25.7.en: By kindness You draw us into the divine embrace.

12.25.8.en: And by firmness You make sin bitter in our mouths.

12.25.9.en: We love You in truth, and we hate sin in truth.

12.25.10.en: * In ignorance the pagans offered human sacrifices to stones.

12.25.11.en: The hearts of mothers and fathers delivered the children to slaughter and burning.

12.25.12.en: The children, unable to defend themselves, became victims of the corruption of their parents.

12.25.13.en: Worship turned into licentious festivals, which know nothing but evil and corruption.

12.25.14.en: Revelry and debauchery ruled over them.

12.25.15.en: And violence and murder gained control over them.

12.25.16.en: You did not destroy them, O wisdom of God, all at once, but You allowed the ruin of one city after another.

12.25.17.en: And in all this You left room for the one who returns to You to be saved.

12.25.18.en: * O wisdom of God, You care for all!

12.25.19.en: You are the God of all, You have no partiality.

12.25.20.en: When Your people sinned in the wilderness they met their end by death.

12.25.21.en: They drank of the waters of the sin that they loved; the cup was filled and they drank it!

12.25.22.en: And in all this You are long-suffering with believers and unbelievers.
